pr_thinkers: Prologue thinker sprites. Animated character sprites used during the prologue historical narrative sequences.
spriteset_aura:
Aura Barrier orbital spriteset (Bank 17, 1544192-1544617 = $17:9000): 3 animations ($00-$02), 12 frame records, 12 sprite groups, 30 sub-sprites. Only user: AuraProjectileChild in attack_ability_system (COP SetMetasprite ( @spriteset_aura )); AuraOrbitalSpawner makes 2 or 4 of those actors (4 when the upgrade flag $0B1E is set) and moves them around the player. The struct format is described in the spriteset_freedan block note.

=== ANIMATIONS ===

| Index | Shape | Played by |
|-------|-------|-----------|
| $00 | 4 frames, hold 7 (8 ticks each), 2 sub-sprites of 8x8 per frame (small sparks) | AnimOnce first, and last when the orbital shrinks |
| $01 | 4 frames, hold 7, 3 sub-sprites per frame (a 16x16 and two 8x8 in the first, three 8x8 in the others) | AnimOnce second, and first when the orbital shrinks |
| $02 | 4 frames, hold 7, 2 sub-sprites of 16x16 (frames 0, 1 and 3) or 4 of 8x8 (frame 2) | the loop that runs until the spawner overwrites the actor's function pointer with AuraProjectileShrink |

AuraProjectileChild stages $00 and $01 once (the orbital grows) and then loops $02; AuraProjectileShrink plays $01 and $00 once and hides the actor ($10 bit $2000). All 12 groups keep the default attack box $F8 $F0 $01 $01.

=== ART AND PALETTE ===

Every tile word is in $0440-$046F: tile numbers $40-$6F with the palette bits (9-11) = 2, i.e. sprite palette 2 (CGRAM $A0-$AF). AuraVramDmaLoader uploads $0600 bytes (48 tiles) of misc_fx_1CC480 to VRAM $4400 with COP AdhocVramDma, and AuraBarrierMain copies 7 colours of fx_palette_198090 to CGRAM $A9-$AF; AuraBarrierPaletteFX cycles bundle #5B over colours $A1-$A8 of the same palette (the bundle writes only $A1-$A8). The statement that VRAM $4400 is tile $40 of the first sprite name table assumes the sprite name base is $4000 (OBSEL not traced).

Byte budget: 426 bytes = 6 (table) + 3 x 18 (lists of 4 records + the hidden $FFFF) + 12 x 13 (group headers) + 30 x 7 (sub-sprites).
spriteset_dark_friar:
Sprite set of the Dark Friar ability effects (Bank 17, 1540096-1541149, 1053 bytes; tile graphics misc_fx_1CC000, uploaded to VRAM $4400 by DarkFriarVramDma, $0480 bytes). The Dark Friar is Freedan's ranged ability; the old note ('fireball travel frames and hit splash') does not fit the code: there is a cast flash, a trail that grows, and spiralling fragments with trail followers. Selected with SetMetasprite ( @spriteset_dark_friar ) in attack_ability_system.

| Index | Set | Frames (hold) | Used by |
|-------|-----|---------------|---------|
| $00 | dark_friar_00_cast_flash | 9 (0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 0) | DarkFriarProjectile: StageSpriteFrame #00, played once (about 20 ticks) |
| $01 | dark_friar_01_trail1 | 3 (0 each) | DarkFriarTrailSouth / DarkFriarTrailEastWest: first trail stage, 2 passes (StageSpriteLoopMoveY / MoveX #01) |
| $02 | dark_friar_02_trail2 | 3 (0 each) | second trail stage, 3 passes |
| $03 | dark_friar_03_trail3 | 4 (0 each) | final trail stage with an active hitbox (StageSprAndHitbox #03) |
| $04 | dark_friar_04_fragment | 4 (1 each; frames 0 1 2 1) | the fragments (DarkFriarFragmentInit: StageSprAndHitbox #04) |
| $05 | dark_friar_05_follower_a | 4 (1 each; frames 0 1 2 1) | TrailFollowerSprA (StageSprAndHitbox #05) |
| $06 | dark_friar_06_follower_b | 4 (1 each; frames 0 1 2 1) | TrailFollowerSprB (StageSprAndHitbox #06) |

Structure (format in the spriteset_freedan block note): 7 animations, 23 groups. 14 B pointer table + 138 B frame lists + 901 B groups = 1053 bytes. Sets $01 and $06 use the same two groups (1783B1, 1783C5), and 178128 is both frame 3 of $00 and frame 2 of $01. Appearance not viewed.
spriteset_darkgaia_projectile:
Sprite set of the Dark Gaia fight projectiles (Bank 17, 1560576-1561583, 1008 bytes). The only user is the four Projectile* actors of player_character (ProjectileSouth/North/West/East), which the Attack* pieces spawn only in scene $E8 (flags $0602); Psycho Dash and Psycho Slide do not use it.

Structure (the sprite-set format is documented once in the spriteset_freedan block note): 8 animations, 12 sprite groups of 9 sub-sprites each (76 bytes per group).

| Index | Set | Frames (hold) | Used by |
|-------|-----|---------------|---------|
| $00 | projectile_launch_south | 3 (5, 2, 2) | ProjectileSouth launch, MoveY #09 |
| $01 | projectile_launch_north | 3 (5, 2, 2) | ProjectileNorth launch, MoveY #0A |
| $02 | projectile_launch_west | 3 (5, 2, 2) | ProjectileWest launch, MoveX #0A |
| $03 | projectile_launch_east | 3 (5, 2, 2) | ProjectileEast launch, MoveX #09 |
| $04-$07 | projectile_travel_south, projectile_travel_north, projectile_travel_west, projectile_travel_east | 1 (9) each | looping travel pose of South/North/West/East, MoveY/MoveX #0F or #10 |

Each travel animation holds a single frame that is the LAST group of its launch animation (e.g. $04 = sprite_group_17D3A4, the last frame of $00), so the projectile keeps its final launch pose while it flies; the 16 frame records therefore use only 12 groups. The ProjectileSouth/North/West/East actors die when they leave the screen, so the travel animation never ends on its own.

Totals: pointer table 16 bytes, frame lists 80 bytes (4 x 14 + 4 x 6), groups 912 bytes. Not traced: the tile graphics these sub-sprites draw.
spriteset_freedan_fx:
Sprite set of two Freedan poses (Bank 17, 1548288-1549554, 1266 bytes): the Aura Barrier cast and the ledge-jump drop attack. The old note ('sword trails, charge flashes', 'attack trail sprites and Dark Friar launch effects overlaid on Freedan') was wrong: the groups are complete body poses of 9 to 14 sub-sprites each, and nothing here belongs to the Dark Friar (that is spriteset_dark_friar). It is body_table row $06 (tile graphics free_fx_1C8000), selected with SetPlayerSpriteDirect #06, which puts it in effect until the next body change.

| Index | Set | Frames (hold) | Used by |
|-------|-----|---------------|---------|
| $00 | freedan_fx_00_drop_fall | 4 (2 each) | LedgeJumpDropAttack (player_character): StageSprAndHitbox #00 while falling |
| $01 | freedan_fx_01_drop_land | 6 (4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 9) | LedgeJumpDropLand: StageSpriteMoveY #01, the landing |
| $02 | freedan_fx_02_aura_cast | 2 (4 each) | Aura Barrier cast (attack_ability_system): StageSpriteFrame #02, played once |
| $03 | freedan_fx_03_aura_sustain | 1 (9) | Aura Barrier sustain: StageSpriteLoop #03, 2 passes and then 10 more while the barrier lasts |

The ledge-jump drop attack is the Freedan-only drop during a ledge jump (CheckLedgeJumpAttack, abilityBitmask bit 6); LedgeJumpDropLand loads entry 2 of freedan_ability_damage_table. The format is documented once, in the spriteset_freedan block note. Each frame is its own group (13 groups, 147 sub-sprites): 8 B pointer table + 60 B frame lists + 1198 B groups = 1266 bytes. The appearance of the tiles was not viewed (OQ-I069-3).
spriteset_shadow_aura_body:
Shadow's Aura body sprites (Bank 17, 1556480-1557571 = $17:C000): 3 animations, 55 frame records, 23 sprite groups, 80 sub-sprites. This is the spriteset of body_table row $08 (art shad_sprites_1BC000, the same tile graphics as Shadow's normal body, spriteset_shadow). Nothing else selects the row: PlayerAuraTransformEntry (player_transition_handlers, entered from item_use_system.UseItem_Aura when Shadow uses the Aura item standing still) calls SetPlayerSpriteDirect #08. The item's own description string is 'Dark Knight Shadow's Body turns to water' (item_description_table $24), which is what these frames show. The old note ('Shadow's unique movement and combat modes') named no code, and the body_table note said that nothing selects row $08; both were wrong.

The struct format (table, frame list, group header, sub-sprite) is described once, in the spriteset_freedan block note.

=== ANIMATIONS ===

| Index | Records | Caller | Content |
|-------|---------|--------|---------|
| $00 | 20 (holds $13, 5, 5, 4, 4, 3, then 13 x 2, then 0) | PlayerAuraTransformEntry: StageSpriteFrame #00 + AnimOnce, first thing after SetPlayerSpriteDirect #08 | 6 groups of 6, 6, 4, 4, 2 and 4 sub-sprites, then 13 groups of 1-7 sub-sprites, then the one-sprite group 17C42F |
| $01 | 19 | PlayerAuraBlockedBySolid (the abort path): StageSpriteFrame #01 + AnimOnce at the original spot, then exit | The same groups as $00 in reverse order (13 small groups, then the 6 large ones, last hold $13), without the final group 17C42F |
| $02 | 16, all hold 0 | PlayerAuraLandAnimLoop: StageSpriteMoveY #02, #01 (Y chain 1 = +1 px per frame) | Alternates the single-sprite groups 17C3DE / 17C3F2 and the four-sprite group 17C406 with the one-sprite group 17C42F every second frame |

The order of the calls is traced; what the frames look like on screen (a body that flattens, rises again, drips) is only read off the shapes: the shrinking sub-sprite counts of $00 and their reversal in $01 match 'turns to water' and the abort that shows the body again, but the art was not viewed (OQ-I071-1). The palette the frames use and where the Aura sequence ends (PlayerAuraTransformExit) are not covered here.

=== CHECKS ===

1091 bytes = 6 (3 pointers) + 3 x 2 (list terminators) + 55 x 4 (records) + 23 x 13 (group headers) + 80 x 7 (sub-sprites). All 23 groups are referenced by the three lists; groups 17C0E8 to 17C1C3 are the six large ones, 17C3DE / 17C3F2 / 17C406 / 17C42F are only used by $02 (17C42F also ends $00).
spriteset_shadow_fx:
Sprite set of body_table row $07 (Bank 17, 1552384-1553318, 934 bytes; tile graphics shad_fx_1CA000). The old note ('Shadow-specific visual effects', 'attack trail sprites and liquify transformation overlays') is not supported: no frame list of this set is staged by any extracted script, because nothing selects body row $07 (SetPlayerSpriteDirect #07 does not occur; the only rows picked by number are $04, $05, $06 and $08). The word 'liquify' appears only in the old header text; no code or table supports it. GetPlayerFacingDirection would index FacingFormOffsetTable with row - 4 = 3 if row $07 were ever selected (OQ-I069-1).

Structure (format in the spriteset_freedan block note): 14 animations, 16 groups of about 5 sub-sprites each (82 in total). 28 B pointer table + 124 B frame lists + 782 B groups = 934 bytes.

| Index | Set | Frames (hold) | Group |
|-------|-----|---------------|-------|
| $00 | shadow_fx_00 | 4 (9, 9, 9, 1) | 17B098, 17B0CF, 17B0FF, 17B12F |
| $01-$03 | shadow_fx_01, 17B034, 17B03A | 1 (3) each | the same group 17B15F |
| $04 | shadow_fx_04 | 8 (3, 3, 3, 6, 4, 3, 2, 0) | 17B18F ... 17B2D1 |
| $05, $07, $08, $0A, $0B, $0D | shadow_fx_05, 17B06E, 17B074, 17B080, 17B086, 17B092 | 1 (31) each | the same group 17B098 (also frame 0 of $00) |
| $06, $09, $0C | shadow_fx_06, 17B07A, 17B08C | 1 (7) each | 17B376, 17B308, 17B33F |

Twelve of the 14 animations are a single frame, and six of those are the identical 32-tick hold of group 17B098 (hold 31 + 1), which looks like placeholder entries (OQ-I069-1). The art was not viewed.
